newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire threatens more air strikes.
newsitem.headline: Zaire threatens more air strikes.

text.p: Zaire's government said on Thursday that it would launch fresh air strikes against enemy positions in the rebel-held east and advised civilians to leave the war zone.

A defence ministry statement, issued as South Africa tried to bring rebel leader Laurent Kabila and President Mobutu Sese Seko's security adviser to the negotiating table, said the army was determined to recapture all enemy held territory.
"The Zairean army is determined to carry on the war, in order to retake all the territory occupied by the invaders," it said.
Zaire accuses neighbouring Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi of invading in support of the rebels, who took up arms in October and hold towns and territory in the east.
"Air raids will be carried out on all fronts until the total destruction of the enemies' military targets," the statement added.
The government forces, who launched a counter-offensive in January hit rebel-held Bukavu, Walikale and Shabunda from the air on Monday. Aid workers reported at least 19 people killed.
Thursday's statement said government infantry were moving towards Walikale and mopping up pockets of resistance there, adding that their goal was to reach the rebel headquarters in Goma.
South Africa threw a news blackout over Thursday's talks.

A government source there said Deputy President Thabo Mbeki was leading a series of separate meetings in his Cape Town office aiming for face-to-face talks between Kabila and Mobutu's nephew and chief security adviser, Ngbada Nzambo Ko Ayumba.
In Kinshasa, Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo told reporters earlier that he had not been informed of such a meeting.
"Until now, I am completely unaware that president Mobutu may have sent any emissary to meet Mr Kabila. I can't say anything. I know nothing about it," he told journalists.
A senior Zairean defence ministry official said there had been no significant development on the war front on Wednesday.
